source: Vinokurova N. Lexical Categories and Argument Structure: A Study with Reference to Sakha. Utrecht, 2005. (LOT Dissertation Series, no. 103)
topic: The low/high opposition in syntactic bundling
notes: Two more pieces of evidence pertain to affix ordering. The first one concerns ordering of the reflexive suffix –n- with respect to the affix –talaa which marks frequentative/distributive aspect. As (31) shows, the reflexive suffix of inalienable possession is closer to the root than the aspectual morpheme which, in its turn, is closer to the root than the reflexive suffix of benefaction.
en: Sardaana washed her face several times.
